public_rationale: The June 2, 2026 executive order directed enforcement against AI-enabled computer crime, but does not establish implementation or subsequent effects (e1). The evidence packet establishes neither a post-publication interval before a qualifying federal response nor substantial AI-linked worsening during that interval (marcus-wake-up-americas-infrastructure-is-e684ca-p1). It therefore supplies no event meeting the contract's early-resolution rule (marcus-wake-up-americas-infrastructure-is-e684ca-p1).
limitations: The earlier enforcement directive does not establish what additional federal action would qualify or whether it occurred.
The packet lacks a comparable publication-date incident baseline and verified post-publication outcomes.
Evaluation occurred on the publication date, November 17, 2026; the forecast has no stated deadline.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI-related cybersecurity and infrastructure problems will get much worse unless and until the federal government acts.
conditions: until the federal government steps up

statement.excerpt: All this is going to get much worse until the federal government steps up, too.
statement.document_title: Wake up! America’s infrastructure is melting. And AI appears to be partly responsible.

from_speaker: is going to get much worse
until the federal government steps up, too
our_interpretation: All this refers to AI-related cybersecurity and infrastructure harms discussed in the surrounding passage.
Much worse means a substantial increase in incident frequency or severity relative to conditions at publication.
The federal government means the United States federal government.
Steps up means a substantive relevant regulatory, enforcement or protective intervention, rather than a statement of concern.
The forecast starts on 2026-11-17 and has no stated deadline.
The conditional exposure is a post-publication interval before a qualifying federal response; its occurrence must be established rather than assumed.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable comparable records show substantial worsening of AI-linked cyber or infrastructure harms after publication and before a qualifying federal intervention, with the absence of such intervention established for that interval.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A qualifying federal intervention closes a documented post-publication interval in which comparable records show no substantial worsening. A temporary lull while the horizon remains open is insufficient.

evidence.excerpt: The Attorney General shall prioritize the enforcement of 18 U.S.C. 1028, 18 U.S.C. 1030, 18 U.S.C. 1343, and all other applicable Federal criminal laws against anyone who utilizes AI to illegally access or damage a computer without authorization, or who utilizes AI while engaged in such illegal access to further any other crime.
evidence.explanation: This primary government disclosure directs enforcement against AI-enabled computer crime before the forecast. It prevents assuming complete federal inaction, but neither establishes implementation nor determines what additional action Marcus meant by steps up.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable, credibly attributed incident records showing substantial worsening after publication and before a verified qualifying federal response, or a qualifying response closing a documented post-publication interval without substantial worsening. Dated federal records must establish the response condition.
